episodes.label: The Weight Loss and the Warning — Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 110: Rimonabant (SR141716A) CB1 Inverse Agonism (PDB 5TGZ), RIO Metabolic Biomarker Gains vs. CRESCENDO Psychiatric Adverse Events & European Withdrawal. In a European clinic in 2008, a man’s weight and blood tests move in the hoped-for direction. The visit changes when he describes how little pleasure he gets from the things he used to enjoy. The Critical Care Clinician follows the measurements and the interview. The Molecular Pharmacologist reconstructs how an antagonist of cannabinoid effects became an inverse agonist in receptor experiments and why a later trial had to count clinical events directly. The patient, dialogue and individual measurements are fictional. Chapter One, “The Endocannabinoid Signaling System in the CNS: A Primer” (2015), in the live Pharmacology notebook introduces SR141716A and inverse agonism. Pharmacology notebook

At the sixth hour of a first fingolimod observation, an atrial impulse reaches the ECG and fails to reach the ventricles. Two weeks later, the lab reports a sharp fall in circulating lymphocytes. episodes.notes: Five-Act historical and biophysical exploration of two intertwined neuropharmacological frontiers: (1) selective alpha-7 and alpha-4-beta-2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor allostery and desensitization in prefrontal cognitive dysfunction (from Loewi, Changeux & Freedman to Cincotta, Yorek MS et al. 2008 and modern PAM/muscarinic therapeutics), and (2) the Wallerian degeneration WldS/SARM1/NAMPT NAD+ survival switch—showing how subclinical pattern-ERG diagnostics after blast-mediated traumatic brain injury identify a therapeutic window where the NAMPT activator P7C3-S243 prevents chronic visual loss (Dutca, Pieper, Harper et al. 2014, PMC5102342) alongside NRK1/2 nicotinamide riboside salvage (Trammell, Brenner et al. 2016, PMC4882590).

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology Pilot 120: Azad Khan's 1977 Sulfasalazine Split Experiment, pH-Dependent Eudragit & MMX Mesalamine Colonic Delivery, Fecal Calprotectin vs. Mucosal Endoscopy & Interstitial Nephritis Surveillance. An oral drug can reach the bloodstream and still deliver little to the tissue it is meant to treat. Mesalamine turns that problem into a historical experiment. First separate the two products of sulfasalazine, then find a way to bring the active one back to inflamed colonic mucosa. The starting source is Chapter Four, *Mucosal Healing in Ulcerative Colitis: Pathophysiology and Pharmacology*, in *Advances in Clinical Chemistry* (2013). A woman’s hip density improved during alendronate treatment. Seven years after she started, a new ache down the outside of her thigh brings her back. Follow the separate paths from a whole-region density measurement to a focal cortical injury, and from an oral tablet to a mineral surface and an enzyme inside an osteoclast. The starting chapter, *Bone and Joints* in the 2013 third edition of *Haschek and Rousseaux’s Handbook of Toxicologic Pathology*, includes alendronate in an ovariectomized rat model and discusses bone remodeling, markers and atypical fractures. A patient with severe pulmonary arterial hypertension becomes breathless after an infusion alarm. The Critical Care Clinician follows the pump log, arterial waveform and pressure on each side of the pulmonary circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows prostacyclin from the original platelet experiment through vinyl ether hydrolysis and receptor signaling. The patient, measurements, timing and dialogue are fictional. episodes.label: Shoulders of Giants — Host Defense & Immunity: Leishmania CXCL1 Proteolysis, Neutrophil CD47/SHP-1 Brakes & CD4 Enhancer Demethylation
episodes.notes: Five-Act immunological detective story tracing three fundamental checkpoints of innate and adaptive immunity: (1) from Mosmann & Coffman's 1986 Th1/Th2 Leishmania major paradigm to selective parasite metalloprotease cleavage of murine CXCL1 (PMC6625741) and the temporal IL-4 instruction paradox (PMC7640617); (2) from motheaten Ptpn6/SHP-1 mutant mice and Weissman's CD47 checkpoint to proving CD47 halts Ptpn6-deficient neutrophils from provoking lethal RIPK1/IL-1 autoinflammation (Science Advances 2023, PMC9821860); and (3) from Littman's Cd4 silencer/enhancer architecture and Rao's TET dioxygenases to stimulus-responsive DNA demethylation sustaining effector CD4 T-cell identity (Nature Communications 2022, PMC8933563).
